newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai central bank says will be no baht devaluation.
newsitem.headline: Thai central bank says will be no baht devaluation.

text.p: A senior Bank of Thailand official said on Thursday that the market need not worry about whether the baht would be devalued following the resignation of Finance Minister Amnuay Viravan.

When asked if there would be a devaluation after Amnuay's departure, the bank's assistant governor, Siri Ganjarerndee, told reporters: "The market is unduly panicking. There is no need to worry (about a devaluation)."

Amnuay on Thursday handed in his resignation to Prime Minister Chavalit Yongchaiyudh after rifts between him and political rivals from within the government's six-party coalition over his handling of the ailing economy.
Amnuay was a hard-liner against the baht's devaluation.
At 0515 GMT, the baht was quoted sharply down at 25.100/25.600 to the dollar in the offshore market compared with 23.530/23.630 late on Wednesday.
In the domestic market, the baht was traded at 25.800/25.900 against 25.850/25.880 late on Wednesday.
Siri said the central bank had no plan to take any action to steady the baht in the offshore market after its fall.
"There is no need to take any action in the offshore market. The central bank will closely monitor the situation in the onshore market," he said.

The heavy buying of dollars in the domestic market significantly squeezed liquidity in the banking system causing the overnight interbank rate to jump to 14-17 percent in the morning from 12.25-12.50 late on Wednesday, dealers said.
